plan.name: Stop Python runners with their sessions
plan.summary: Bind every Python application runner to the session that launched it, so completion, failure, cancellation, timeout and Close leave no running runner or lifetime helper; Close must cancel and join an active invocation instead of waiting indefinitely for it. Install an independent process watchdog before application imports, carrying fresh session liveness through the existing private mounts, so loss of the session owner or a local runner's parent stops the runner within five seconds even while Python loops, sleeps or C code holds the GIL, including when a surviving launcher or Docker daemon hides the owner's death. Fail closed if lifetime protection cannot start or fails, clean up and reap its helpers on ordinary exits, and preserve literal command arguments, isolation, normal outcomes, session reuse, portable fingerprints and the existing module-step watchdog and deadline rules. Add process-level regression coverage for startup and cleanup failures, normal and failed runs, cancellation, deadlines, concurrent Close and owner SIGKILL, with real Docker coverage under the existing Python execution opt-in as well as local coverage. Update SPEC.md and docs/python.md to describe this lifetime guarantee, citing [#934's ratified plan](.invariant/plans/issue-934.json) in SPEC.md; this plan records the reversible extension of the existing session policy in D-0181 and D-0183 and preserves D-0356 and D-0438.

tests.name: TestPythonApplicationExecutionCancellationLeavesNoRunner934
tests.says: Normal and failed runs retain their outcomes, and cancelling or expiring a running invocation stops its real Python runner even when cancellation kills only the local launcher.

tests.name: TestPythonApplicationExecutionCloseStopsRunner934
tests.says: Closing an active session cancels its invocation, stops its runner and returns promptly; repeated Close is safe and a closed session cannot run again.

tests.name: TestPythonApplicationExecutionOwnerDeathStopsRunner934
tests.says: Killing the process holding a prepared session stops its runner within five seconds, even with a surviving intermediate launcher and a driver blocked during import or holding the GIL.

tests.name: TestPythonApplicationExecutionParentDeathStopsRunner934
tests.says: A runner whose immediate parent dies stops independently within five seconds even while its session owner and execution resources remain alive.
